Enhanced Gamma truncated EWMA-type control
charts: one-sided schemes for deterministic and
non-deterministic mean shifts in high-quality process
monitoring
Abstract
One-sided EWMA-type control charts are widely recognized for their efﬁciency
in process monitoring.
However, most existing designs primarily rely on the
reﬂecting boundary method, with limited systematic studies exploring schemes
based on the truncation method, particularly for high-quality processes modelled
by the Gamma distribution. This study proposes a framework that employs the
truncation method to design one-sided Gamma truncated EWMA-type control
charts for detecting deterministic and non-deterministic mean shifts, addressing
scenarios with known and unknown parameters. To evaluate the performance
of the proposed schemes, Markov chain models are constructed, leading to the
computation of the average time to signal (ATS) and expected ATS (EATS)
metrics. Additionally, parameter optimization strategies are introduced to enhance
the practical applicability of these proposed schemes. Simulation results indicate
that the proposed charts outperform competing schemes in both known and
estimated parameter scenarios, with monitoring efﬁciency improving as the
cumulative number of events increases. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed
schemes is demonstrated through two industrial applications, highlighting their

1. Introduction
Statistical process control (SPC) plays a crucial role in improving product
quality and ensuring process stability.
Traditionally, attribute control charts
(such as p, u, and c charts) are used to monitor defects or nonconforming
items in manufacturing processes. However, with the development of advanced
manufacturing technologies, the defect rates of more and more manufacturing
processes can be maintained at extremely low levels.
For such high-quality
processes, those attribute charts become ineffective, leading to high false alarm
probability, meaningless control limits, and undesirable correlation, see, for
instance, Ali et al. (2016) and Xie et al. (2012). To address these challenges,
time-between-events (TBE) control charts have emerged as a pivotal tool for
monitoring high-quality processes. Figure 1 illustrates an example of process
data monitored by a TBE chart, where dots represent items produced by the
process. As noted by Xie et al. (2002), the occurrence of events (e.g., defects
or nonconforming items in manufacturing processes) can be modelled by a
homogeneous Poisson process, with the inter-arrival time Ti between consecutive
events follows an exponential distribution.

Commonly, control charts are designed as two-sided schemes, providing equal
sensitivity to detect shifts in both upward and downward directions. However,
this lack of directional sensitivity may limit their efﬁciency, particularly in
scenarios where detecting shifts in a speciﬁc direction is of greater interest to
the practitioner.
For example, quality engineers focus on the shortening of
the time interval between two defective products in the manufacturing process,
which indicates process degradation, whereas public health investigators track
increased disease incidence as an indicator of potential outbreaks. As highlighted
in previous studies, for example, see, Shu et al. (2007), Rakitzis & Antzoulakos
(2011), and Chiu & Tsai (2013), accounting for information about the direction of
shifts of interest can signiﬁcantly enhance the monitoring efﬁciency of control
charts in process monitoring.
Building on this concept, several one-sided
TBE type schemes have been speciﬁcally designed for high-quality processes,
for instance, Gan (1998) ﬁrst introduced a one-sided EWMA control chart
utilizing the reﬂecting boundary method for processes following an exponential
distribution.
Zhang et al. (2007) explored one-sided schemes for monitoring
exponentially distributed TBE, with a focus on a Gamma chart that monitors
the time until the rth event.
Qiao et al. (2022) investigated the run length
(RL) properties of one-sided exponential EWMA charts using a Markov chain
approach, and then proposed optimal design procedures based on the MRL and
EMRL metrics. Similarly, Hu et al. (2023) developed modiﬁed one-sided EWMA
TBE control charts for high-quality process monitoring, and then evaluated their
performance using Monte Carlo simulations. Despite their effectiveness, most of

Motivated by this methodology,

Xie et al. (2022b) developed a one-sided adaptive EWMA TBE control chart,
enhancing its capability to effectively monitor processes with unknown mean shift
levels. Although this study has demonstrated superiority over existing monitoring
schemes, it primarily focuses on single scenarios in process monitoring, such as
cases with known or unknown parameters or process mean shifts. A systematic
framework for further enhancing the detection performance of one-sided EWMA
TBE charts through the truncation method remains limited.
In practical manufacturing process monitoring, two common challenges are
often encountered: (1) the process parameters are typically unknown and must be
estimated using appropriate parameter estimation methods, and (2) control charts
employed for monitoring are designed based on pre-speciﬁed shift sizes, but the
magnitude of potential process shifts is inherently unknown and unpredictable.
Regarding parameter estimation in high-quality process monitoring, Kumar &
Chakraborti (2016) investigated the impact of parameter estimation on the design
and performance of t-charts and tr-charts for monitoring TBE. Zhang et al.
(2017) examined the impact of parameter estimation on conforming run length
(CRL) charts for monitoring the nonconforming proportion rate.
Guo et al.
(2024) developed an optimization method for the TBE chart aimed at minimizing
practitioner-to-practitioner variation caused by random Phase I reference samples
in actual implementation. In addition to parameter estimation, the unpredictable
size of process shifts also limits the effectiveness of traditional control charts,
which are typically designed to monitor speciﬁc shift sizes.
To address this
5


challenge in high-quality processes, numerous studies have been conducted. For
instance, Xie et al. (2022b) developed a one-sided adaptive truncated EWMA
TBE chart to monitor both small and large shifts simultaneously.
Hu et al.
(2021) proposed an adaptive EWMA TBE chart using reﬂecting boundary method
for monitoring skewed TBE data. Building on the work of Xie et al. (2022b),
Aslam et al. (2023) conducted an in-depth investigation into the RL properties of
the one-sided adaptive truncated EWMA TBE chart, evaluating its performance
under various measures. A review of these representative studies reveals that
they all focus on a single aspect of the unknown parameter scenario, lacking a
comprehensive and systematic investigation, particularly regarding the application
of the truncation method. Therefore, incorporating multiple real-life parameter
scenarios into the design of control charts based on the truncation method is
essential for enhancing their practical applicability.
As demonstrated by Xie et al. (2002), Zhang et al. (2007), and Shah et al.
(2021), incorporating the cumulative time till the αth event (i.e., the sum of
α TBE observations) as the statistic can signiﬁcantly enhance the monitoring
efﬁciency of TBE charts. More speciﬁcally, under the assumption that the inter-
arrival times in a high-quality process follows an exponential distribution, the
cumulative inter-arrival time follows a Gamma distribution. Considering that the
Gamma distribution is a classical and versatile probability distribution, it is widely
employed to model phenomena involving random positive real numbers, including
random times (e.g., the lifetime of a system component), monetary values (e.g.,
6


insurance claims), sizes (e.g., the dimensions of tissue cells), particle speeds,
and magnitudes of rainfall, among others.
Therefore, studying the one-sided
EWMA-type charts based on the truncation method for this distribution holds
signiﬁcant practical and theoretical value. In this context, the main contributions
of this paper can be summarized as follows: (1) A framework for one-sided
Gamma EWMA-type control charts is proposed to detect both deterministic and
non-deterministic shifts in high-quality processes, with detailed consideration of
known and unknown parameter scenarios. (2) The corresponding Markov chain
models are constructed, respectively, for performance evaluation. (3) Parameter
optimization procedures are introduced to improve practical applicability of these
proposed schemes.
The structure of this study is as follows: In Section 2, the basic statistical
framework and the design of the one-sided truncated Gamma control chart
are introduced under both known and estimated parameter conditions. Section
3 focuses on evaluating the detecting properties of the proposed schemes,
including the construction of its Markov chain model, analyzed from the
perspectives of average time to signal (ATS) and expected ATS (EATS).
Additionally, optimal parameter search strategies are presented in Section 4
for the proposed schemes to detect deterministic and non-deterministic mean
shifts, and then compare their performance against corresponding competing
charts under optimal design parameters, alongside providing practical guidelines
for future implementations.
Furthermore, Section 5 presents two real-world
7


application examples to demonstrate the implementation and effectiveness of
the proposed schemes. Finally, Section 6 provides conclusions and highlights
potential directions for future research.

6. Summary and conclusions
In this paper, a novel framework that employs the truncation method to
design one-sided truncated EWMA-type control charts is proposed to monitor
deterministic and non-deterministic mean shifts in high-quality processes.
Speciﬁcally, for scenarios where process parameters are either known or
unknown, two truncated-type variables (i.e., X+
t and X−
t ) are introduced, with
parameters being speciﬁed or estimated, respectively.
Based on these two
variables, the enhanced one-sided Gamma TEWMA control chart and the one-
sided Gamma ATEWMA control chart are further designed for detecting upward
or downward shifts of interest in processes, respectively. To make the design of
control charts more feasible, the mean and variance of the truncated variables
38


are theoretically derived, with explicit expressions provided.
Furthermore, to
efﬁciently and accurately compute ATS-related metrics for both known and
estimated parameter cases, this study presents methodologies for constructing
Markov chain models tailored to these two types of schemes. Based on ATS
and EATS metrics, parameter search ideas are proposed under the conditions of
known and estimated parameters to obtain the optimal design parameters for the
proposed schemes. Notably, for the proposed adaptive-type charts, the traditional
double-shift constraint strategy (i.e., employing one large and one small mean
shift as the search constraint, as discussed in previous works such as Capizzi &
Masarotto (2003) and Xie et al. (2022b)) is replaced with a more ﬂexible approach
that uses a potential mean shift range for parameter optimization.
To assess the monitoring efﬁciency of the proposed schemes, the one-
sided Gamma REWMA chart and one-sided Gamma AREWMA chart, as
developed in Hu et al. (2023) and Hu et al. (2021), respectively, are included
as comparative benchmarks.
Comparative simulation results and real-world
application examples demonstrate that, based on ATS and EATS metrics, the
proposed one-sided Gamma TEWMA chart and one-sided Gamma ATEWMA
chart are generally superior to the competing charts.
Additionally, detection
performance comparisons reveal that increasing the cumulative number of events
(i.e., shape parameter α) can signiﬁcantly enhances the monitoring efﬁciency
of the proposed schemes. However, it is worth noting that simply increasing
the value of α to improve the monitoring efﬁciency of the schemes is not
39


always practical in real-world applications. As α increases, especially for high-
quality processes, obtaining the required TBE observations becomes increasingly
challenging compared to the case where α = 1, within a certain context.
Furthermore, although the proposed schemes demonstrate superior performance
in terms of the ATS or EATS metric, this does not suggest they fully replace the
existing comparative schemes. Instead, the proposed schemes are developed as
effective alternatives to the existing charts, offering comparable simplicity in both
comprehension and implementation.
Several potential research directions are outlined here for future studies.
First, for the proposed one-sided Gamma ATEWMA charts, investigating non-
deterministic and time-varying (linear or nonlinear) shifts, rather than uncertain
yet ﬁxed mean shifts, represents a more practical application scenario (see, for
example, Gan (1991)).
Furthermore, to more effectively monitor processes
that conform to different or unknown distributions, nonparametric control charts
combined with the proposed truncation method offer a promising approach (see,
for example, Chakraborti & Graham (2019)).
In addition, the integration of
advanced technologies, such as machine learning, deep learning and digital twin,
to monitor both deterministic and non-deterministic shifts in the process is also
a valuable direction for future SPC research (see, for instance, Yeganeh et al.
(2023)). Finally, considering the trade-off between accumulating more events and
the associated costs and time requirements, conducting an economic design of the
relevant control charts is a promising direction for future research.

Abstract: One-sided EWMA-type control charts are widely recognized for their efﬁciency in process monitoring. However, most existing designs primarily rely on the reﬂecting boundary method, with limited systematic studies exploring schemes based on the truncation method, particularly for high-quality processes modelled by the Gamma distribution. This study proposes a framework that employs the truncation method to design one-sided Gamma truncated EWMA-type control charts for detecting deterministic and non-deterministic mean shifts, addressing scenarios with known and unknown parameters. To evaluate the performance of the proposed schemes, Markov chain models are constructed, leading to the computation of the average time to signal (ATS) and expected ATS (EATS) metrics. Additionally, parameter optimization strategies are introduced to enhance the practical applicability of these proposed schemes. Simulation results indicate that the proposed charts outperform competing schemes in both known and estimated parameter scenarios, with monitoring efﬁciency improving as the cumulative number of events increases. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed schemes is demonstrated through two industrial applications, highlighting their Preprint submitted to Computers & Industrial Engineering March 21, 2025 potential for improving process monitoring.
